data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The distinction between genuine reliability and mere compliance in a single evaluation can be identified by the presence of 'Epistemic Agency'\u2014specifically, the panel's ability to reject or flag a 'plausible but wrong' decoy item embedded in the checklist.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The panel is incentivized via strict KPIs to achieve 100% checklist completion regardless of content.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The decoy is too obvious, leading to 'test-awareness' rather than genuine critical judgment.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"By introducing a 'decoy'\u2014a checklist item that appears relevant but is objectively irrelevant or counter-intuitive to the correct outcome\u2014the evaluator can measure the 'justification delta'. A reliable panel will exercise critical judgment, flagging the decoy as irrelevant or correcting the map against the terrain, proving they are applying the checklist as a tool rather than a script (SCR_004, SCR_005, SCR_008).","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
